item.title: Scientists Discover First Adult T. Rex Trackway with Human-Sized Footprints
item.description: Scientists have discovered the first known trackway made by an adult Tyrannosaurus rex, a significant find that provides insight into the behavior and movement of this iconic dinosaur. The trackway, found in North Dakota, consists of four footprints measuring approximately 1 meter (3.2 feet) in length and up to 0.80 meters (2.6 feet) in width, spaced about 4 meters (13.1 feet) apart. The footprints, preserved in calcium carbonate, date back to 66.5 million years ago, just before the asteroid impact that led to the extinction of non-avian dinosaurs. Researchers estimate the T. rex was walking at a speed of 1.5 to 2 meters per second (3.3 to 4.5 miles per hour), which is comparable to the average human walking speed. This discovery is particularly significant because, despite numerous T. rex skeletal remains, only a few isolated footprints had been previously identified, mostly from juvenile specimens. item.title: Updated Data Reveals 2,300 Immigrants Departed Minnesota Following Winter Immigration Surge
item.description: According to updated federal data obtained by the Deportation Data Project, a winter surge of 3,000 federal immigration agents to Minnesota resulted in over 2,300 immigrants leaving the country. The new total includes 2,019 explicitly recorded deportations and 315 immigrants who left after being arrested but without clear detention records. This represents approximately 2% of Minnesota's estimated undocumented population of around 130,000 as of 2023. The data, which covers arrests from December 1 to February 15, shows most arrests occurred in January during the peak of the operation. Over 3,600 arrests were recorded during this period, with most deportations happening between December and February, though over 400 occurred after February. item.description: The founder of one of Arizona's largest charter school networks, Glenn Way, CEO of Charter One LLC and chairman of the Educational Freedom Fund PAC, is under criminal investigation for allegedly funneling corporate funds to 25 Republican state legislative candidates through his political action committee. item.title: Astronomers Identify Unusual X-Ray Sources Emitting Low-Energy Radiation and Ultraviolet Light
item.description: NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory has identified a new type of celestial object that exhibits unique characteristics not previously observed. The discovery involves compact binary systems in which a compact object, such as a black hole, neutron star, or white dwarf, steals gas from a companion star. Unlike typical compact binaries that emit high-energy X-rays during this accretion process, these newly discovered objects emit very low-energy X-rays while producing significant amounts of ultraviolet radiation. The research team, led by Mustafa Muhibullah of the University of Alabama, detected 84 such objects across six galaxies, including four evolved elliptical galaxies and two spiral galaxies (the Andromeda Galaxy and the Pinwheel Galaxy). These objects have been termed 'hypersoft X-ray sources' due to their weak X-ray emissions. item.title: Perl Developers Can Now Build Interactive Web Interfaces Using Server-Driven UI Technology
item.description: WebForms Core (WFC) is a server-driven UI technology that allows Perl applications to generate commands for manipulating the browser's DOM without requiring a separate frontend framework. The article demonstrates how WFC can be integrated with Perl and the Mojolicious framework to create interactive web interfaces. The core concept involves a server-side 'Commander' (WebForms class) that generates UI commands, which are then executed by a browser-side 'Executor' (WebFormsJS). This approach differs from traditional methods where JavaScript frameworks handle UI manipulation. The article provides detailed examples, including a memory card game implemented entirely in Perl with Mojolicious and WFC. The memory game example shows how server-generated commands can handle complex interactions like card matching, move counting, and game state management without requiring a separate frontend application. item.title: Aircraft Actuator Electrification Transforms System Architecture in Modern Aviation
item.description: The article discusses the ongoing shift from hydraulic systems to electric actuators in aircraft, a trend known as 'more-electric aircraft' (MEA) systems. This transformation is redefining the system-level architecture of aircraft, moving away from traditional hydraulic components that have been used for decades. The article explains that hydraulic systems, while reliable, are complex, heavy, and require significant maintenance due to their reliance on fluid pressure, piping, valves, and pumps. In contrast, electric actuators offer several advantages including better fault localization, easier maintenance, and the ability to provide real-time feedback for improved performance. item.title: UK state pension set to rise 3.9%, pushing payments above the income tax threshold
item.description:
The UK state pension is expected to increase by 3.9% next year after official wage-growth data were released by the Office for National Statistics. The increase is based on the government's triple-lock system, under which the state pension rises by whichever is highest among average wage growth, inflation, or 2.5%. Average weekly earnings increased by 3.9% between May and July, making that figure the likely rate for the next pension increase. The final rate will depend on the inflation figure used in the calculation, but it is expected to be below 3.9%.
If confirmed, the full new state pension would increase by about £479 a year, from £12,547.60 to approximately £13,036.60. That would put the annual payment above the current £12,570 personal income tax allowance by roughly £467, meaning part of the state pension could become taxable for many recipients. item.description: A consortium of pharmaceutical companies has demonstrated that incorporating proprietary protein structure data into AI models significantly improves their performance in predicting protein-drug interactions. The AISB model achieved high accuracy on more than half of 1,056 test protein-ligand structures, compared to one-third for the publicly available OpenFold3 version and around 40% for another open-source model. item.description: Despite King Mohammed VI’s position as head of state, a powerful inner circle effectively runs Morocco. item.title: Federal Judge Blocks Kennedy Center from Restoring Trump's Name on Building Exterior
item.description: A federal judge has ruled that the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts cannot honor President Donald Trump with an inscription on the building's exterior. U.S. District Judge Christopher R. Cooper issued the ruling on Tuesday, blocking the president's hand-picked board from restoring Trump's name after an earlier order forced its removal. The judge stated that the board cannot install memorials for Trump or anyone else without Congress's approval, emphasizing that the board's resolution violates a federal court order and a statute enacted by Congress. The Kennedy Center's board had initially added Trump's name to the building's formal title in December 2025, crediting him with securing $257 million for a renovation. However, Judge Cooper ruled in May that the renaming was unlawful, as only Congress has the authority to authorize such changes, and ordered the removal of the name. The center complied with the order while appealing the decision. Last month, the board attempted to circu

item.title: Study reveals FOXA1-CYP4Z1 axis as key regulator in breast cancer lipid metabolism
item.description: A recent study published in Scientific Reports has uncovered a significant molecular mechanism in breast cancer progression involving the FOXA1-CYP4Z1 axis. The research demonstrates that FOXA1, a transcription factor, suppresses breast cancer development by downregulating CYP4Z1, a member of the cytochrome P450 family. CYP4Z1 was found to be markedly overexpressed in breast cancer tissues and strongly correlated with poor patient prognosis. Functional experiments showed that silencing CYP4Z1 inhibited cancer cell proliferation, migration, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition while promoting apoptosis and senescence. Conversely, overexpression of CYP4Z1 enhanced malignant behaviors in breast cancer cells. Lipidomics analysis revealed that CYP4Z1 downregulation disrupted lipid homeostasis, particularly by inducing triglyceride accumulation, highlighting its critical role in maintaining tumor lipid metabolism. item.title: Israel's Far Right Proposes Seven-Year Plan for Gaza Displacement
item.description: Israel's National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, leader of the Jewish Power party, has unveiled a seven-year plan called 'Disengagement 710' aimed at facilitating the 'voluntary migration' of Gaza's population to countries such as Turkey, Ethiopia, and Congo. The plan calls for the departure of approximately 250,000 people in the first year, 1.11 million within three years, and 1.86 million within seven years, which would encompass most of Gaza's population. Ben-Gvir's proposal includes creating a new ministry dedicated to 'voluntary migration,' complete with a minister, director-general, budget, and international negotiating team. The plan is presented as a solution to the ongoing conflict, with Ben-Gvir stating, 'Instead of illusions of peace now, we need actions of emigration now.' However, Gazans interviewed by RT reject the initiative as illegal under international law and a crime against humanity. item.title: FBI Records Reveal Anonymous Donor Paid for Cremation of Trump Attempted Assassin
item.description: The New York Post reported that an 'anonymous donor' paid for the cremation of Thomas Crooks, the gunman who attempted to assassinate former President Donald Trump at a July 2024 rally in Butler, Pennsylvania. This detail was buried in documents provided to Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley (R-IA) as part of his inquiry into the assassination attempt. The documents included a note at the end of an FBI interview summary with Crooks' father, Matthew Crooks, indicating that an anonymous donor covered the cremation costs. Matthew Crooks, described as retired and his wife on leave from work, reportedly lacked the financial means for funeral arrangements. Matthew also stated he was unemployed at the time of the shooting. The revelation was first made public in 2024 by Rep. Clay Higgins (R-LA), who expressed outrage over the FBI releasing Thomas' body to the family within two weeks of the attack. item.title: US AI Labs Face Debate Over Distilling Frontier Models for Smaller, More Efficient Systems
item.description: The article discusses a debate within the AI community regarding whether US-based open-weight AI labs should be allowed to distill frontier models to create smaller, more efficient models. The controversy arises as frontier AI companies like Anthropic and OpenAI are pushing back against the practice of distilling their models, calling it 'illicit' and 'theft,' while simultaneously using similar techniques themselves. The article highlights that distillation is a common practice in AI development, where smaller models are trained using the outputs of larger models. This process, known as model distillation, is seen as a way to make AI more accessible and efficient. However, frontier labs argue that distillation violates their terms of service and could lead to security risks. The article also points out the irony that these companies have been training their models on vast amounts of publicly available data without proper compensation, yet now they are claiming that distilling their mod

item.title: Trump Claims Security Guard Avoided Death in Kennedy Center Ceiling Collapse During Renovation Push
item.description: President Donald Trump has continued his campaign to gain more control over the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, claiming that a security guard narrowly avoided death due to the building's poor condition. The incident in question involved a small section of ceiling collapsing in a heavily trafficked hallway at the Kennedy Center earlier this month, though no injuries were reported. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick initially stated that the ceiling fragment had 'missed one of the Center's security guards by just minutes' and could have 'killed' numerous patrons. Trump expanded on this claim in a lengthy post on his social media platform, Truth Social, where he argued that the building's state of disrepair necessitated his increased involvement in its management. He wrote, 'A large piece of concrete and steel just dropped down, in a thud, from the ceiling of a heavily trafficked main hallway. item.title: FBI Director Kash Patel Faces Scrutiny Over Claimed Statistics on Crime Reduction
item.description: FBI Director Kash Patel faced criticism during a congressional hearing for citing statistics that former FBI Deputy Director Andrew McCabe and CNN's Evan Perez described as questionable. Patel, President Donald Trump's nominee, presented data to counter Democratic criticism of his leadership, but McCabe and Perez questioned the validity of the numbers, particularly regarding the FBI's role in reducing crime rates. McCabe noted that many of the statistics Patel referenced, such as a 500 percent increase in enforcement actions and claims of 1,100 thwarted terrorist attacks, were not accurate or within the FBI's jurisdiction. Perez highlighted that some statistics, like declining carjacking rates, do not fall under the FBI's core responsibilities, making it inappropriate for the FBI to claim credit for such trends. McCabe also criticized Patel's assertion about changes to hiring policies to 'protect victims of bestiality,' calling it bizarre and irrelevant, as he could not recall the term

item.title: How to Accurately Compare Google Trends Data in Spreadsheets Without Misinterpreting Search Interest
item.description: The article discusses a method for comparing Google Trends data in spreadsheets without confusing relative interest scores with actual search volumes. The author, who is building a tool called CleanScrape, explains that a Google Trends value of 100 does not represent 100 searches but rather a relative interest score within the comparison. The article provides a step-by-step guide using an Apify Actor to extract Google Trends data for terms like 'ChatGPT' and 'Claude' in the US over a three-month period. The process involves inputting specific JSON parameters to request interest-over-time data, which is then exported as a CSV or Excel file. The author emphasizes the importance of keeping both search terms in the same request to avoid separately normalized series that would make comparisons difficult. item.title: Police Departments Use Flock Surveillance System with Inappropriate Search Reasons
item.description:
According to a report by 404 Media and the Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF), law enforcement officers across multiple jurisdictions have been using Flock's surveillance search engine to track license plates and locations with inappropriate, nonsensical, or humorous reasons. The EFF's analysis revealed that officers frequently entered phrases such as 'LMAO,' 'IDK,' 'Hehe,' 'Asdfg,' 'dickhead,' 'shithead,' and even 'robbery I don't remember the case number leave me alone' into the 'reason' field when conducting searches. Some officers simply left the field blank or used generic terms like 'investigation' or 'test.'
The report highlights that these searches were conducted across more than 19,000 cameras in 1,558 cities and towns, with records showing hundreds of thousands of searches performed. The EFF argues that this casual approach to a powerful surveillance system demonstrates a lack of accountability and a disregard for constitutional privacy safeguards. The system, which allows

item.title: Flow Neuroscience's FDA-Approved Headset Offers Non-Pharmaceutical Depression Treatment in US
item.description: Flow Neuroscience has launched its FDA-approved headset for depression treatment in the United States, marking a significant development in mental health care. The device, which delivers low-intensity electrical stimulation to the left frontal lobe of the brain, is designed to be used at home for 30 minutes daily via a mobile app. This approach targets the same brain region affected in depression, where reduced activity and weaker neural connections are common. The device received FDA approval in December 2025, positioning it as an alternative to traditional antidepressant medications, which are taken by approximately one in six American adults. While the device costs $2,200 for a 10-week treatment period followed by $325 monthly thereafter, it offers a non-pharmaceutical option that could potentially reduce reliance on antidepressants. item.title: CBS News' '60 Minutes' Premiere Shows Significant Viewership Decline Under New Editor-in-Chief
item.description: The premiere of CBS News' '60 Minutes' for its first full season under editor-in-chief Bari Weiss has shown a significant decline in viewership compared to previous years. According to early Nielsen data reported by the New York Post, the show drew approximately 7.7 million viewers for its season opener, marking the smallest premiere audience since at least 2000. This represents a 19 percent drop in total viewership and a 33 percent decline in the key 25-to-54 demographic compared to the previous year's premiere. CNN's Brian Stelter reported on BlueSky that preliminary numbers indicate the premiere could be down more than 20 percent year-over-year, with the previous season's premiere drawing 10 million viewers. A TV executive cited a weaker NFL lead-in this year and Nielsen methodology changes as contributing factors, though the executive noted it would still be 'a pretty striking drop.' item.title: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Rep. Maxine Waters Clash Over Inflation and Debt During Financial Services Committee Hearing
item.description: During a House Financial Services Committee hearing on September 15, 2026, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent faced intense questioning from Ranking Member Maxine Waters (D-CA) regarding inflation and fiscal policy. Waters pressed Bessent for direct answers on whether tariffs have contributed to rising inflation, asking, 'If tariffs are not inflationary, as you claimed in your previous testimony, then why has inflation increased by more than 3% over the past year?' Bessent repeatedly avoided providing a clear response, leading to a heated exchange where he snapped, 'You're not making sense!' Waters, who was given the floor for her five-minute questioning period, continued to challenge Bessent on the administration's economic policies, particularly the record $40 trillion national debt under President Trump's leadership. She criticized the administration for failing to reduce deficits as promised, instead delivering higher costs for American households. Earlier in the hearing, Waters had

item.title: Roman Empire's Road Network Reveals Other Cities Were Better Connected Than Rome
item.description: A new study published in Nature Communications on September 15, 2026, challenges the common saying that 'all roads lead to Rome.' Researchers from Aarhus University in Denmark, led by Professor Tom Brughmans, have conducted extensive research on the Roman Empire's road system, revealing that several other cities were better connected by road than Rome itself. The study, part of a larger digital atlas project called 'Itiner-e,' mapped nearly 186,000 miles (300,000 kilometers) of Roman roads. The findings indicate that major cities like Antioch, Ancyra (modern-day Ankara), Byzantium (modern-day Istanbul), and Corinth were better connected to the road network than Rome. The research identified the empire's 'most important intermediary route' by land, which did not run through Rome but followed the North African and Levantine coast past Antioch and near Ankara, crossed over to Europe at Constantinople, and moved through the Po Valley and Milan into France. item.title: Former TikTok Executives Launch AI-Powered App to Guide Users in Taking Better Selfies
item.description: A new iOS application called Superpose, developed by former TikTok executives Melody Chu and Jing Liu, has been launched to help users improve their photography skills through AI guidance. The app, which was released in July 2026, allows users to take selfies or photos of friends and generates four AI-assisted pose suggestions. Users can save these poses or use the 'match pose' feature to align themselves with the suggested framing. The app offers five free pose generations per day, with additional packs available for purchase at $2.99 for five or $9.99 for 20. Chu, who previously worked at Meta, TikTok, and Slack, explained that the idea stemmed from her personal frustration with her husband's poor photography skills. She aimed to solve this problem using advancements in computer vision and generative AI. Superpose has already been downloaded over 22,000 times, with users generating more than 190,000 poses. item.title: Orange County Holds First-Ever E-Bike Buyback Event Amid Safety Concerns
item.description: Orange County authorities recently held a groundbreaking e-bike buyback event, modeled after gun buyback programs, which drew significant public interest and some criticism. The event, organized by the Orange County district attorney’s office, offered gift cards ranging from $200 to $1,000 for surrendered e-bikes, e-scooters, and e-motorcycles. Nearly 1,000 vehicles were collected, filling nine 26-foot U-Haul trucks, with participants lining up as early as midnight. The program, funded by asset forfeiture funds and an additional $5,000 from Orange County Supervisor Katrina Foley, aimed to remove potentially dangerous e-bikes from the streets. District Attorney Todd Spitzer emphasized that the initiative was part of a broader strategy to address e-bike-related safety issues, including child endangerment charges against parents who allowed underage riders to use inappropriate e-motorcycles. item.description: Wichita, Kansas - Three days after President Donald Trump threatened to ban sales of Canadian jet manufacturer Bombardier in the United States, employees at the company's U.S. headquarters in Wichita expressed strong opposition to the president's remarks. An employee, who wished to remain anonymous, walked out of the company's headquarters and spoke to a reporter after ensuring no one was nearby. The employee stated that the president's comments felt like a betrayal of American workers, particularly in a state that has historically supported Republican candidates. The Washington Post article, published on September 14, 2026, highlights the backlash from Bombardier workers in Wichita, a city known for its significant aerospace industry presence. item.description: FBI Director Kash Patel faced questioning from Senator John Kennedy (R-LA) during a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing on September 15, 2026, regarding the FBI's policy on bestiality in agent applicant screenings. The exchange occurred after a grilling from Senator Dick Durbin (D-IL) on the topic. Senator Kennedy expressed confusion about why bestiality was being discussed in the context of hiring FBI agents, stating that such issues have 'really hurt the FBI' by creating perceptions that political views matter more than qualifications. Patel clarified that the FBI automatically disqualifies individuals who participated in bestiality, emphasizing that the agency would not hire 'criminals.' item.title: Trump's Arctic Commission Chair Raises Conflicts of Interest and Foreign Policy Concerns
item.description: The U.S. Arctic Research Commission, which has historically advised Congress and the president on Arctic research and policy, has become a focal point of controversy following President Donald Trump's appointment of Thomas Dans, a Texas venture capitalist and MAGA influencer with no scientific background, as its chair. Dans, who has no formal expertise in Arctic science or policy, has leveraged his position to advance personal business interests, particularly with Damen Shipyards, a Dutch shipbuilder with which he has a prior business relationship. His advocacy for Damen's icebreaker projects, including a potential U.S. government contract, has raised ethical concerns, as Dans is not required to disclose conflicts of interest under federal ethics rules due to his non-employee status. The White House has defended Dans, stating he is "doing a great job" and that his shipbuilding expertise benefits the commission. item.title: Cher, Elton John and other stars pay tribute to legendary designer Bob Mackie
item.description:
Legendary costume and fashion designer Bob Mackie has died at age 87, prompting tributes from generations of entertainers whose careers and public images were shaped by his work. Cher, Elton John, Miley Cyrus, Sabrina Carpenter and Pink were among the stars who publicly honored the designer, whose glamorous creations became a defining part of American entertainment and popular culture.
Known as the “Sultan of Sequins,” Mackie was celebrated for elaborate costumes featuring sequins, feathers, beads, rhinestones and dramatic silhouettes. His long career included collaborations with some of the biggest names in music and television, including Dolly Parton, Tina Turner, Diana Ross, Madonna, Beyoncé and Pink. He also designed costumes for The Carol Burnett Show throughout its 11-year run from 1967 to 1978 and created distinctive fashions for Barbie dolls beginning in the late 1980s.

item.description: Political analysts Krystal Ball and Saagar Enjeti have raised concerns about an imminent U.S. economic downturn, citing a combination of Middle East geopolitical tensions and a potential slowdown in the artificial intelligence sector. The analysts highlighted recent developments in the Middle East, including the Houthis gaining control of the Bab al-Mandeb Strait—a critical global shipping route—and damage to the Saudi Arabian East-West oil pipeline, which threatens 4% of global oil supply. These developments have contributed to surging oil prices, described by Ball as 'extraordinarily dire,' amid ongoing disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. Enjeti warned that the U.S. economy, heavily reliant on AI-driven tech investments accounting for about half of real GDP growth since 2025, faces a potential 'freefall' if the AI industry slows down while inflation from Middle East conflicts continues to rise. The suspected assailant, 19-year-old Conoray Lawantara, a Beverly Hills resident, was charged with murder and pleaded not guilty. item.description: A New York University mathematics professor, Tristan Buckmaster, has accused OpenAI of copying his work on a fluid dynamics equation, specifically the Euler problem, which is a stepping stone to solving the Navier-Stokes problem. Buckmaster, who was collaborating with Levent Alpöge from Anthropic, claims that OpenAI scientists approached him to jointly announce a solution to the Navier-Stokes problem after becoming aware of his research. He questions how OpenAI could have solved the problem so quickly, noting that the timing coincided with their awareness of his work. OpenAI's website announcement credited their AI model Astra with solving the Navier-Stokes proof, stating no user data was incorporated, though they acknowledged anonymized data might have been used to improve their models. item.title: Fay Wray’s 1920s Fashion: A Study of Hollywood’s Transition from Flapper to Elegant Silhouettes
item.description: The article presents a collection of 40 vintage photographs showcasing the fashion styles of Canadian-American actress Fay Wray during the late 1920s. Wray, who would later become famous for her role in the 1933 film 'King Kong,' was a brunette starlet under contract with Paramount Pictures during this period. The photographs highlight her signature style that captured the transition of fashion in the late 1920s (1928-1929), where silhouettes began shifting from the boxy shapes of the mid-1920s to more fluid, elongated elegance. Wray's wardrobe featured classic late-1920s gowns with dropped waistlines, delicate silk crepes, satin, and soft pleating. As the decade closed, her style evolved toward bias-cut gowns that hugged natural curves while maintaining an elongated line. Her signature look included ultra-fitted cloche hats pulled low over the brow, often embellished with fabric flowers or subtle metallic brooches. item.description: President Donald Trump has publicly criticized the U.S. Supreme Court for its recent rulings, particularly regarding mail-in voting regulations, in a 463-word post on Truth Social. The president accused the justices of political cowardice and claimed the court's decisions have set America back 'at least a hundred years.' item.description: First Lady Melania Trump has distanced herself from reports that a Russian oligarch, Umar Kremlev, helped finance the wedding of her son Donald Trump Jr. and his second wife, Bettina Anderson. According to a statement from Melania's representatives to The Daily Mail, she has no relationship with Kremlev and played no role in organizing the wedding or its financial planning. item.description: The article discusses photographer Luca Battaglia's series titled 'Ticket non remboursable' (Non-Refundable Ticket), which captures traditional carousels across European city squares through long exposure photography. Battaglia uses heavy neutral density filters and exposures lasting up to 30 seconds to create ethereal images where the carousels blur into radiant bands of color and light while the surrounding city remains sharp and still. The article explains that Battaglia's work is deeply personal, as he grew up in Milan with fond memories of a neighborhood carousel that eventually disappeared. He began seeking out carousels not just as nostalgic attractions but as living hubs of memory and shared public life. The photographs show carousels in various European cities including Honfleur, Toulouse, Bercy in Paris, Deauville, Tikkimäki, Dijon, Tuileries in Paris, Grenoble, Charles Michels in Paris, Nice, and Marseille. item.description: Newly disclosed FBI documents, provided to Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley (R-IA) as part of his inquiry into the July 2024 shooting in Butler, Pennsylvania, detail years of increasingly strange behavior by Thomas Matthew Crooks, the gunman who attempted to assassinate President Donald Trump. item.title: Accenture settles U.S. government DEI allegations with $25 million payment
item.description: Accenture, an IT consulting firm, has agreed to pay $25 million to settle allegations from the U.S. government regarding its diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) practices. The settlement, announced on Monday, involves the U.S. Department of Justice and Accenture, and specifies that the company will pay $25,000,000, including civil penalties and interest at a rate of 4% per annum from September 9, 2026. The Trump administration has targeted DEI practices in its second term, penalizing both public and private organizations for diversity initiatives that civil rights advocates argue help address historic inequities for marginalized groups such as women, the LGBT community, and ethnic minorities. The White House has characterized DEI as anti-merit and discriminatory against white people and men, leading to executive orders requiring federal contractors to eliminate DEI programs. item.title: New World Screwworm Returns to U.S., Threatening Livestock and Wildlife
item.description: The New World screwworm, a flesh-eating parasite that was eradicated from the United States in the 1950s, has made a comeback, reaching Texas and New Mexico. This parasitic fly's larvae feed on living tissue, causing severe wounds in livestock, wildlife, pets, and occasionally humans. The University of California San Diego, in collaboration with the County of San Diego Health and Human Services Agency, has developed a new tracking dashboard to predict where the parasite might strike next. The dashboard integrates confirmed detections, environmental conditions, and media reports to provide real-time risk assessments for counties across the country. Launched in 2023, the program aims to help coaches recognize unconscious gender biases and stereotypes that negatively affect girls' experiences in sports. item.title: Senate Bill Aims to Regulate Cryptocurrency Sector Amid Trump Family Wealth Concerns
item.description: The U.S. Senate is preparing to vote on the Clarity Act, a bill designed to regulate the cryptocurrency sector, which has reportedly generated over $1.4 billion for the Trump family in 2025 alone. Critics argue that the legislation fails to address potential conflicts of interest and could even facilitate further enrichment for the Trump family through their crypto ventures. Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) criticized the bill on the Senate floor, calling its ethics provisions a 'fig leaf' that would not prevent Trump from making additional profits. item.title: Penang Mandates Covered Walkways for Transit-Oriented Development Projects
item.description: Penang developers are now required to construct covered walkways and pedestrian links around transit stations under new regulations aimed at prioritizing public access and connectivity over property density. Jason H'ng Mooi Lye, chairman of Penang's local government and town and country planning committee, emphasized that Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) does not permit developers to seek higher density or plot ratios. Instead, TOD focuses on creating connectivity and essential public facilities to ensure easy access to LRT stations, bus stops, taxi stands, and other future transit infrastructure. H'ng highlighted that Penang Island City Council (MBPP) has already implemented covered walkway requirements for certain developments, even outside designated TOD zones, to address existing connectivity gaps. item.title: Democrats Expand Recruitment Program to Include Independent Candidate in Alaska
item.description: With less than 50 days until Election Day, House Democrats are adding new candidates to their top recruits list — including one who isn't actually a Democrat. The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee (DCCC) announced Tuesday that it is expanding its 'Red to Blue' program, which offers candidates strategic guidance, staffing, and fundraising help, to include Bill Hill, an independent running for Alaska's at-large House seat, along with Michigan Democrat Will Lawrence and Wisconsin Democrat Mitchell Berman. The additions bring the program's total to 40 candidates for the cycle. Hill, a fisherman and former school superintendent, finished second behind the Republican incumbent in Alaska's nonpartisan primary and won the state Democratic Party's endorsement after committing to support organized labor and abortion rights. item.title: Bodega Peptides Tested Fail to Contain Actual Peptide Ingredients
item.description: WIRED conducted an investigation into the peptide products sold at bodegas, particularly focusing on the viral trend of peptides marketed for various health benefits. The publication purchased four types of peptides from Mr. Green, a Brooklyn bodega, and sent them to an independent testing lab. The results revealed that the samples did not contain the active peptide ingredients listed on their labels. Instead, the vials were found to be mislabeled or degraded, containing little more than water or saline solution. The testing showed low levels of heavy metals and endotoxins, suggesting they were not actively harmful, but the absence of the claimed ingredients meant the products were ineffective. item.title: Correcting the Typography of Botanical Names on Websites
item.description: The article discusses a common mistake in how websites format botanical names, specifically the incorrect use of italics. Most websites wrap entire plant names in italics, but according to botanical naming conventions (ICN for wild plants and ICNCP for cultivated ones), only certain parts should be italicized. The genus, species epithet, and infraspecific epithets should be italicized, while rank markers (such as subsp., var., f.), author citations, hybrid signs (×), cultivar groups, and cultivar names (which go in single quotes) should not be italicized. For example, 'Hosta 'Blue Angel'' should be formatted as Hosta 'Blue Angel' with only 'Hosta' italicized. The author noticed this error on their plant app, PlantGeekz, while building a library for botanical names. The article explains that plant names often arrive in inconsistent formats from various sources, such as spreadsheets, nursery catalogs, and user input, with issues like incorrect symbols (x instead of ×), misspelled abbrevi

item.title: Buzkashi: The Ancient and Fierce Traditional Sport of Tajikistan
item.description: Buzkashi, known as 'goat pulling' in Persian, is an ancient and fiercely contested sport deeply rooted in Tajikistan's cultural heritage. The sport, which has been played for centuries among the nomadic horse cultures of Central Asia, involves riders competing to seize and hold the headless carcass of a goat, aiming to drag it across a goal line marked by scattered hay. Unlike modern team sports, Buzkashi has no formal teams, boundaries, or referees, creating a chaotic and mythic spectacle that echoes historical cavalry charges. The game is played in vast open fields, often in remote valleys, and is central to Tajik cultural gatherings such as weddings, seasonal festivals, and rites of passage. It is not merely preserved as a heritage activity but is actively lived and experienced by the community. The process relies on accessing state voter websites using personal information such as birth dates and partial Social Security numbers, which may violate state laws. DHS attorneys reportedly told agents they would not be personally liable for these searches if properly documented, but watchdog group Democracy Defenders argues that accessing these websites could still have legal implications. The whistleblower also raised concerns about the accuracy of the data used, noting that it includes identification numbers for noncitizens who have become naturalized citizens, potentially leading to fal

item.title: Kansas Town Becomes Site of Underground Nuclear Reactor for AI Power Needs
item.description: The article discusses a nuclear experiment in Parsons, Kansas, where a small town with one in five residents living in poverty is becoming the site of the first underground nuclear reactor designed to power artificial intelligence. The reactor is being drilled through an aquifer on land where the Army still detonates waste explosives under federal permit. The article highlights that the nuclear industry is seeking locations where 'nobody gets a vote' to avoid public opposition, and Parsons, Kansas, fits this description due to its high poverty rate and lack of political influence. The article references a report from the Kansas City Defender dated September 9, 2026, which details the situation. The piece is part of a broader discussion on nuclear issues, including the history of nuclear disasters, environmental concerns, and the role of nuclear power in the context of AI development. The article also touches on the broader implications of nuclear energy for climate change, renewable en

item.title: Senate Leader McConnell's Office Collects Nearly $1 Million in Pay During Absence
item.description: According to a recent report by The Daily Beast, Senator Mitch McConnell (R-KY), the 84-year-old Senate Minority Leader, has been absent from Capitol Hill since being hospitalized from his Washington, D.C., home on June 14, 2026, missing over 60 recorded Senate votes. Despite his absence, McConnell and his staff have continued to receive taxpayer-funded pay. The report states that McConnell earned $43,500 in taxpayer-funded paychecks during his 92-day absence, while the six highest-paid members of his staff collectively received $318,688 before taxes. The entire staff received approximately $893,872, bringing the office's total payout—including McConnell's salary—to about $937,000. McConnell, who is not seeking reelection, continues to earn approximately $476 for every day he remains away from the Senate. Media reports indicate that he is expected to reappear on Capitol Hill as the Senate prepares to reconvene on Monday. The article highlights the financial implications of his prolonge

item.title: Irán avanza en el Parlamento con proyecto para retirarse del Tratado de No Proliferación Nuclear
item.description: El Parlamento de Irán ha avanzado con una iniciativa para retirar al país del Tratado de No Proliferación Nuclear (TNP), una decisión que modificaría el marco internacional bajo el cual Teherán mantiene sus compromisos de control y supervisión atómica. La propuesta, presentada ante la Mesa del Parlamento, busca ser tratada con máxima urgencia y requiere la autorización del presidente del Parlamento, Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf, antes de llegar al recinto para su debate. El diputado Hossein Ali Haji Deligani confirmó que varios legisladores respaldan una propuesta de tres puntos para formalizar la salida iraní del tratado, vinculándola con los ataques estadounidenses e israelíes contra instalaciones iraníes y con las recientes acciones internacionales relacionadas con el expediente nuclear de Teherán. Ebrahim Azizi, presidente de la Comisión de Seguridad Nacional y Política Exterior del Parlamento, afirmó que la opción está sobre la mesa y que existen proyectos preparados para avanzar hacia

item.title: Agresión al vehículo de la diputada Julia Ferreras en Ceuta tras confusión sobre apoyo a ETA
item.description: En el puerto de Ceuta, decenas de personas destrozaron el coche de la diputada Julia Ferreras y del activista Rafael Borrego, miembro de la Flotilla, tras confundirlos con personas que apoyarían a ETA. El incidente ocurrió cuando un audio difundido en redes sociales, que afirmaba que 'apoyan a ETA', generó una reacción violenta entre un grupo de personas que se manifestaban en el puerto. Durante el ataque, Ferreras y Borrego informaron a los agresores que eran diputada y ciudadana de Ceuta, pero no lograron detener la violencia. Los atacantes proferían amenazas y los dos se sintieron en peligro, llegando a pensar que no podrían salir de la situación. Un agente de la policía logró sacar el vehículo del lugar, conduciéndolo hacia el garaje privado de la diputada. La diputada Ferreras denunció que los agresores no cesaron en su violencia a pesar de las aclaraciones, y que sintió miedo por su integridad física. El audio que desencadenó el incidente fue difundido por un grupo de extrema der

item.title: Abascal justifica agresión contra militantes de izquierda con gritos homófobos y redes rechazan su postura
item.description: El líder de Vox, Santiago Abascal, ha sido cuestionado sobre una agresión ocurrida en Oviedo contra dos militantes de izquierda, en la que los atacantes profirieron insultos como "rojos de mierda", "maricones" y "Arriba España", considerada un delito de odio por la Policía Nacional. En lugar de condenar la acción, Abascal aseguró que las víctimas habían pedido que expulsaran a su partido de la ciudad y que "a la gente que hace eso, luego le pasan estas cosas". Esta declaración ha generado una fuerte reacción en las redes sociales, donde muchos usuarios han criticado su postura, señalando que no está condenando la violencia sino justificándola. Un usuario escribió: "Vox sigue justificando la violencia", mientras que otro comentó: "Abascal no condena: justifica. Por si quedaba alguna duda sobre la motivación de odio". La comunidad de Twitter también ha propuesto soluciones como aplicar la ley de partidos a Vox, con frases como "Si no condenan la violencia la consecuencia es bien sencilla

item.title: El lanzamiento de jabalina de Miguel de la Quadra-Salcedo: un récord mundial anulado por cambios en el reglamento
item.description: Miguel de la Quadra-Salcedo, atleta español reconocido por sus logros en el lanzamiento de jabalina, estableció un récord mundial 'fantasma' en 1956 que fue posteriormente anulado por la IAAF. El atleta, quien también destacó como reportero de guerra, periodista y aventurero, perfeccionó una técnica innovadora conocida como 'estilo español' o 'la jabonosa', que implicaba giros sobre sí mismo antes de lanzar la jabalina, aumentando significativamente la distancia. En una exhibición en una aldea española, logró lanzar la jabalina hasta 112,30 metros, superando en casi 30 metros la marca mundial de la época. La IAAF, presionada por países nórdicos y para los Juegos Olímpicos de Melbourne, prohibió la técnica poco antes de los Juegos, modificando el reglamento para que el lanzamiento no pudiera realizarse de forma rotatoria. Los registros previos, incluido el de Quadra-Salcedo, fueron anulados, a pesar de que los cambios en el reglamento no eran retroactivos. España, que boicoteó los Juego

item.title: Una finca autorizada antes de la dana se construye junto al cauce del barranco entre Albal y Catarroja
item.description:
Una nueva finca residencial situada junto al barranco de la Font de la Rambleta, entre Albal y Catarroja, ha vuelto a poner el foco sobre las construcciones en zonas con riesgo de inundación tras la dana del 29 de octubre de 2024. El edificio, ubicado en el Camí Real, en el tramo de Albal denominado avenida Padre Carlos Ferris, cuenta con licencia municipal concedida antes de la riada y las obras comenzaron también antes del episodio de lluvias. Cuando se produjo la inundación, los cimientos y buena parte de la estructura ya estaban ejecutados.
El inmueble se encuentra prácticamente terminado y todas las viviendas han sido vendidas. Sus plantas, incluidos los bajos, tienen ventanas orientadas directamente hacia el cauce del barranco, una zona que sufrió los efectos de la riada de 2024 y donde se localizaron víctimas arrastradas por la corriente. Los vecinos del entorno también han padecido históricamente problemas relacionados con el desbordamiento de colectores procedentes de Albal.

item.title: Rufián critica duramente a Mazón por su actitud durante la investigación sobre la DANA de 2024
item.description: El portavoz de ERC en el Congreso, Gabriel Rufián, ha realizado duras críticas contra el expresidente de la Comunidad Valenciana, Carlos Mazón, durante la comisión del Congreso que investiga la gestión de la DANA de 2024, que provocó 232 muertos. Rufián expresó su indignación al ver a Mazón con 'buena cara' y 'moreno' mientras se presentaba como víctima de la DANA, a pesar de que durante la emergencia se encontraba en un reservado durante cinco horas mientras la población sufría las consecuencias. El diputado de ERC señaló que Mazón 'no merece ni un minuto de atención' y lo calificó de 'negligente, inútil, homicida imprudente y psicópata'. Mazón, por su parte, defendió su posición afirmando que el único poder que podría juzgar su responsabilidad penal ya se había pronunciado en su favor, exonerándolo de responsabilidad. Destacó que el Tribunal Superior de Justicia había descartado su responsabilidad por unanimidad de cinco jueces de diferentes posiciones ideológicas. Rufián, sin embarg

item.title: Nuevo desprendimiento en el Palacio de los Hurtado de Mendoza de Almazán afecta cubierta y columnas
item.description: El Palacio de los Hurtado de Mendoza, ubicado en Almazán (Soria), ha sufrido un nuevo desprendimiento esta noche del domingo 20 de septiembre de 2026, alrededor de las 21:30 horas. Según informó el alcalde de la localidad, Jesús Cedazo, el colapso ocurrió en la misma zona y fachada que ya se había visto afectada en un desprendimiento anterior a principios de este mes. El desprendimiento afectó a parte de la cubierta del edificio y a columnas laterales, según las primeras impresiones del regidor. El Ayuntamiento de Almazán ha movilizado a los equipos correspondientes y ha informado a las autoridades autonómicas, incluyendo a técnicos y a Patrimonio, así como a la delegada de la Junta de Castilla y León. El alcalde adelantó que mañana se evaluarán los daños para determinar si se ha afectado al torreón y otros departamentos del palacio. Este nuevo incidente se suma al grave desprendimiento ocurrido a principios de septiembre, que provocó el derrumbe de dos plantas en la zona central, dest

item.title: Pareja de 50 años rehabilita siete masías abandonadas durante un siglo en el Alt Empordà
item.description: Una pareja de 53 y 56 años, Carme y Martí, ha decidido rehabilitar siete masías abandonadas desde hace casi 100 años en una finca del Alt Empordà, en Cataluña. El proyecto, que busca conservar la historia y estructura original de las construcciones, no pretende convertir las masías en viviendas nuevas disfrazadas de antiguas, sino mantener elementos como muros, arcos y piedra original. Las siete masías, que llevaban entre 80 y 100 años deshabitadas y en distintos estados de ruina, no conservan sus cubiertas originales, lo que aceleró el deterioro de muros y forjados. La interiorista Silvia Mallafré, responsable del proyecto, explica que cada masía tiene un grado de deterioro y una historia constructiva distintos, por lo que no existe una solución estándar. El trabajo implica desmontar, limpiar y clasificar la piedra original para volver a incorporarla a la obra, conservando grandes rocas del terreno que forman parte físicamente de las construcciones. Además, se incorporan criterios de

item.title: Carlos Mazón se niega a declarar ante la comisión del Congreso sobre la DANA, argumentando que un tribunal ya lo exoneró
item.description: El expresidente valenciano Carlos Mazón ha decidido no hacer declaraciones públicas ante la comisión del Congreso que investiga la DANA (Desastre de la Albufera de Noviembre) hasta que concluya la instrucción judicial de la tragedia ocurrida el 29 de octubre de 2024. Durante su comparecencia, Mazón justificó su decisión afirmando que un tribunal ya se había pronunciado en su favor, exonerándolo de cualquier responsabilidad. En su intervención, Mazón destacó que el Tribunal Superior de Justicia había emitido un auto en el que se descartaba por completo su responsabilidad, aunque no aclaró que se trató de un auto y no de una sentencia firme. A pesar de su negativa inicial a declarar, Mazón respondió a las preguntas de varios diputados. En particular, cuando el diputado de EH Bildu Mikel Otero le preguntó si asumió el mando de la emergencia durante la riada, Mazón respondió que no, ya que la normativa de emergencia lo prohibía. La diputada de Compromís Águeda Micó le acusó de ser responsa

item.title: El Banco de Tejidos CIEN: cerebros donados para investigación en enfermedades neurodegenerativas
item.description: El Banco de Tejidos CIEN (BT-CIEN), ubicado en el Centro Alzheimer de la Fundación Reina Sofía en Madrid, es un biobanco especializado en muestras neurológicas que recibe donaciones de cerebros de personas con enfermedades neurodegenerativas, así como de personas sanas. Fundado en 2010, este banco combina la extracción, procesamiento y diagnóstico neuropatológico de los cerebros donados con la investigación y cesión de muestras a investigadores externos, siempre dentro del marco ético y legal establecido. El neuropatólogo Alberto Rábano, director científico del BT-CIEN, destaca que el trabajo del banco contribuye al desarrollo de la medicina de precisión en enfermedades neurodegenerativas, como el Alzheimer, el Parkinson y las demencias. La donación de cerebros permite estudiar directamente el órgano afectado, relacionando los cambios observados en el cerebro con la historia clínica del paciente. El BT-CIEN cuenta con un programa de donación interno vinculado al Centro Alzheimer y otro

item.title: El consumo de agua con gas aumenta en España como alternativa al alcohol entre los jóvenes
item.description: La noticia analiza cómo el alcohol está enfrentando una crisis generacional en España, lo que está impulsando un crecimiento significativo en el consumo de agua con gas. Según datos presentados en la publicación, el volumen de ventas de aguas con gas en España creció un 14,3% interanual en 2025, alcanzando 202,7 millones de litros vendidos. En los supermercados, el crecimiento fue aún más pronunciado, del 21,4%, convirtiendo a las aguas carbonatadas en la categoría que más crece en el sector de las bebidas 'sin'. El Informe de consumo alimentario de 2025 del Gobierno español revela que el consumo per cápita de agua con gas en 2025 fue de 2,5 litros por persona, frente a los 60,4 litros de agua sin gas. Los analistas señalan que esta tendencia se relaciona con la búsqueda de alternativas más saludables a las bebidas alcohólicas, especialmente entre los jóvenes de entre 18 y 24 años, cuyo consumo de alcohol ha disminuido aproximadamente un 60% en las últimas dos décadas. El Ministerio de

item.title: Ayuso inyecta 340.000 euros en 'The Objective' en cinco años a pesar de sus pérdidas continuas
item.description: La Comunidad de Madrid, liderada por la presidenta Isabel Díaz Ayuso, ha inyectado 340.000 euros en el medio digital 'The Objective' durante un periodo de cinco años, según revela la información publicada por El Salto. Este importe se reparte de la siguiente manera: 14.500 euros en 2021, 35.000 euros en 2022, 56.500 euros en 2023, 116.250 euros en 2024 y 117.140 euros en 2025. En los últimos dos años, la cantidad alcanzó los 234.000 euros. El medio, dirigido por Álvaro Nieto y con Paula Quinteros como directora general, ha acumulado pérdidas significativas desde su fundación en 2013, con un total de aproximadamente 7,4 millones de euros en pérdidas desde 2017 a 2025. A pesar de estas pérdidas, 'The Objective' ha recibido financiación pública a través de contratos publicitarios por parte de la Comunidad de Madrid, lo que ha permitido al medio evitar la quiebra. El artículo señala que el medio no ha publicado críticas sobre temas sensibles como el ático adquirido por la Comunidad de Madr

item.title: La Audiencia Nacional amplía la investigación contra mandos israelíes por torturas en el abordaje de la Flotilla de la Paz
item.description: La Audiencia Nacional ha admitido dos querellas contra mandos militares israelíes por la detención ilegal de tripulantes de la Flotilla de la Paz, una acción que se produjo en el mar Mediterráneo en 2010. Estas querellas, presentadas por organizaciones de derechos humanos, buscan responsabilizar a altos mandos israelíes por posibles crímenes de guerra y torturas cometidas durante el abordaje de la flotilla que intentaba romper el bloqueo de Gaza. El juez de la Audiencia Nacional ha solicitado a la Fiscalía de la Corte Penal Internacional que decida si incluye los hechos relatados en las querellas en algún procedimiento actualmente en curso. Además, el magistrado ha pedido a la Fiscalía que se pronuncie sobre si los hechos cometidos a bordo de las embarcaciones de bandera española pueden ser investigados por la Audiencia Nacional de manera separada e independiente de los hechos que investigue la Fiscalía de la Corte Penal Internacional. Mientras tanto, el juez ha advertido que continuar

item.title: La innovadora maniquí de tela para el parto creada por Angélique Marguerite Le Boursier du Coudray en el siglo XVIII
item.description: En el siglo XVIII, el parto seguía siendo una experiencia aterradora y a menudo mortal para las mujeres y los recién nacidos en Europa. Muchas mujeres y bebés fallecían debido a la falta de conocimientos médicos y cuidados especializados. En este contexto, Angélique Marguerite Le Boursier du Coudray emergió como una figura transformadora y valiente. Nacida en 1712, se convirtió en una de las comadronas más respetadas de Francia en un momento en que pocas mujeres tenían acceso a una educación formal. Sin embargo, en lugar de limitarse a su práctica privada, du Coudray se propuso formar a otras personas para llevar técnicas seguras de parto a las zonas más desfavorecidas del país. Con el apoyo del rey Luis XV en 1759, du Coudray inició una campaña nacional para educar a comadronas y cirujanos rurales. Durante más de dos décadas, viajó de pueblo en pueblo, enseñando habilidades prácticas de parto mediante demostraciones y conferencias. Lo más revolucionario de todo fue su invención de un

item.title: Windows 11 implementa nueva herramienta de restauración que recupera el estado del sistema y optimiza el almacenamiento
item.description: Windows 11 ha introducido una nueva herramienta de recuperación llamada Point-in-time restore, diseñada para devolver el equipo a un estado anterior eliminando cambios del sistema operativo, archivos personales y aplicaciones instaladas después de ese punto. A diferencia de la tradicional 'Restaurar sistema', esta función trata el equipo como un todo, sin distinguir entre archivos personales y configuración del sistema. La herramienta se activa por defecto en la mayoría de equipos y genera un punto de control cada 24 horas, conservando estos puntos durante 72 horas antes de eliminarlos automáticamente. En las ediciones Enterprise de Windows 11, el intervalo de creación de puntos puede reducirse a 6 o 4 horas. La configuración de almacenamiento para esta función se puede ajustar en Configuración > Sistema > Recuperación > Point-in-time restore, permitiendo definir el espacio máximo que puede ocupar. Para usar la herramienta, es necesario arrancar el equipo en modo de recuperación y acce

item.title: Mujer de 54 años se quita la vida tras ser desahuciada de su vivienda en L'Hospitalet
item.description: Una mujer de 54 años de L'Hospitalet de Llobregat, Barcelona, se suicidó el 7 de septiembre de 2026, cinco meses después de haber sido desahuciada de su vivienda en el barrio de Santa Eulàlia, donde había residido más de veinte años. Olga, madre de dos hijas (una de ellas menor), había comprado el piso hace más de dos décadas con una hipoteca del Banco Sabadell. Tras separarse y perder su trabajo, no pudo hacer frente a los pagos hipotecarios. Acordó con el banco que la entidad se quedara con el piso a cambio de poder vivir allí pagando un alquiler social, lo que mantuvo hasta que el inmueble fue vendido a Promontoria Real Estate, un fondo de inversión que inició el proceso de desahucio. La noche antes del desahucio programado para el 15 de abril, Olga amenazó con quitarse la vida, activándose el protocolo antisuicidio y siendo trasladada de urgencia al Hospital de Bellvitge. Su abogado solicitó frenar la ejecución, pero el juez decidió continuar, argumentando que la familia actuaba co

item.title: Denuncian la declaración de cuatro macrogranjas porcinas en Codo pese a los problemas de abastecimiento de agua
item.description:
La organización Stop Ganadería Industrial ha denunciado que el Ayuntamiento de Codo, localidad zaragozana de 204 habitantes, declaró de interés público cuatro explotaciones porcinas promovidas por Explotaciones Ganaderas Estiche, filial del grupo Cincaporc. La decisión fue aprobada el 4 de septiembre en un pleno extraordinario, según la organización, que sostiene que los vecinos no fueron informados previamente y que el consistorio todavía no ha respondido a su solicitud de acceso a la documentación que justificaría la declaración.
Las cuatro instalaciones proyectadas comprenden dos explotaciones de cebo, con capacidad para 6.000 y 7.200 animales, y dos explotaciones destinadas a la producción de lechones, con 864 unidades de ganado mayor cada una. Stop Ganadería Industrial señala que tres de los proyectos se situarían en el límite máximo permitido para este tipo de instalaciones en suelo rústico.
De acuerdo con las estimaciones aportadas por la organización a partir de los proyectos

item.title: Inspector de la Policía Nacional denuncia falsificación de informes por parte de la Brigada de Estupefacientes
item.description: El artículo relata la denuncia presentada por un inspector de la Policía Nacional, conocido como 'el policía de los millones emparedados', quien afirma que la Brigada de Estupefacientes ha estado creando informes falsos y ocultándolos a los tribunales. Según el informe, el inspector, quien se encuentra en prisión preventiva, ha revelado que la Brigada de Estupefacientes, parte de la Policía Nacional, ha estado manipulando documentos para respaldar investigaciones y acusaciones contra individuos, incluyendo a él mismo. El inspector, cuyo nombre no se revela, ha sido acusado de corrupción y se le han encontrado millones de euros en efectivo en su domicilio, lo que ha llevado a su arresto. Sin embargo, el inspector sostiene que los informes falsos fueron creados para justificar su detención y para encubrir la corrupción dentro de la propia brigada. La investigación se centra en la Brigada de Estupefacientes, que es responsable de combatir el tráfico de drogas y otros delitos relacionados.

item.title: Secuestro en Montornès del Vallès: asaltantes imitan a policías para llevarse a víctima en AP-7
item.description: Un grupo de individuos vestidos como agentes de la Policía Nacional han protagonizado un secuestro en la autopista AP-7, en el término municipal de Montornès del Vallès. Según informa Metrópoli Abierta, los hechos ocurrieron el sábado a las 19:30 horas, cuando dos vehículos colisionaron ligeramente. Tras el accidente, cinco personas salieron de uno de los coches y se dirigieron al otro vehículo con pasamontañas y chalecos reflectantes que imitaban a los de la Policía Nacional. Los asaltantes sacaron a la fuerza a una persona del asiento trasero del vehículo, la arrastraron por la autopista y la metieron en su automóvil. La víctima fue liberada horas después, según confirmaron las fuentes policiales. Los Mossos d'Esquadra, la policía catalana, están investigando el caso para localizar a los responsables. La noticia destaca que los individuos se hicieron pasar por autoridades para llevar a cabo el secuestro, lo que representa un caso de delincuencia que ha generado preocupación en la zon

item.title: Escritor marroquí defiende en El País la devolución de Ceuta y Melilla a Marruecos como paso histórico
item.description: El diario El País ha publicado un artículo de opinión firmado por el escritor marroquí Tahar Ben Jelloun que propone la entrega de Ceuta y Melilla a Marruecos, calificándola como 'un gesto histórico y realista'. El autor sostiene que estas ciudades autónomas, situadas en territorio marroquí, constituyen una 'aberración anacrónica' en el siglo XXI, al igual que Gibraltar en territorio español. Ben Jelloun vincula la propuesta con la crisis migratoria ocurrida en Ceuta los días 30 y 31 de julio, que dejó 141 muertos en el mar, y considera que este evento ha resucitado la cuestión territorial de manera 'violenta'. El artículo defiende la postura del presidente Pedro Sánchez, quien ha intentado mantener buenas relaciones con Marruecos, y critica a la oposición española, especialmente a partidos como el Partido Popular y Vox, por sus críticas al gobierno y por supuestos actos de racismo contra migrantes marroquíes. Ben Jelloun también exculpa al régimen de Mohamed VI de la entrada masiva de

item.title: Airbus en huelga | AL LÍO - YouTube
item.description: La noticia proporcionada no contiene información sustancial sobre una huelga de Airbus. El contenido mostrado es únicamente el título de un video en YouTube, junto con información genérica sobre derechos de autor, contacto, creadores, publicidad y términos de servicio. No hay detalles sobre la huelga, los motivos, las fechas, los sindicatos involucrados o cualquier otro elemento que permita elaborar un resumen periodístico. El texto proporcionado es meramente un encabezado de video sin contenido real, lo que impide generar un resumen válido. La información es insuficiente para determinar si se trata de una noticia real o si hay algún conflicto laboral en curso. El título menciona 'Airbus en huelga', pero no se proporciona ningún detalle adicional que respalde esta afirmación. Por lo tanto, no es posible elaborar un resumen periodístico de más de 300 palabras como se solicita.

item.title: El Parlamento Europeo pospone la votación del acuerdo comercial con Marruecos tras la crisis migratoria en Ceuta
item.description: El Parlamento Europeo ha decidido posponer la votación del acuerdo comercial con Marruecos, que incluye los productos del Sáhara Occidental, debido a la crisis migratoria en Ceuta. El acuerdo, firmado en 2025 por la Comisión Europea y los Veintisiete, se encuentra en aplicación provisional y requiere la ratificación del Parlamento Europeo para ser definitivo. La resolución aprobada en Estrasburgo el pasado jueves calificó los hechos del 30 y 31 de julio como 'una invasión' y responsabilizó a Marruecos por la avalancha migratoria. La reforma del acuerdo comercial incluye preferencias arancelarias para frutas y hortalizas del Sáhara Occidental y un mecanismo de etiquetado que no distingue entre productos saharauis y marroquíes. Además, propone un intercambio anual de información en el Comité de Asociación para evaluar cómo llegan los beneficios comerciales a la población saharaui.
